weekend_note: The week looks dry and sunny, with highs in the upper 80s through Friday, then a breezy cooldown into the mid 70s this weekend (north winds gusting to about 35 mph late Friday). The bigger issue is Isaias recovery: ECUA's boil-water notice is still countywide, Escambia schools, UWF and Pensacola State are closed today, and city parks were asked to be avoided until cleared. Treat outdoor events as unconfirmed until organizers say otherwise. Picks are the Blue Angels practice on Oct 14, Gallery Night and Beach-O-Ween on Oct 16, Ice Flyers on Oct 17 (indoors at the Bay Center) and Barktoberfest on Oct 18.

news.title: FPL expects most Escambia power back by Tuesday
news.summary: FPL said Monday that about 70 percent of Escambia and Santa Rosa customers should have power by the end of that day and the rest by the end of Tuesday, Oct 13. Over 300,000 customers across Northwest Florida had been restored, with roughly 17,000 line workers from 29 states on the job.

news.title: Escambia recovery update: boil-water notice, closures and debris pickup
news.summary: ECUA's boil-water notice remained countywide Monday, and Pensacola Beach has its own notice. Escambia public schools, Pensacola State and UWF are closed Tuesday, Oct 13. County storm debris collection is targeted to start Oct 14, and residents are asked to stay out of parks until cleared.

news.title: City of Pensacola reports power returning and meal sites open
news.summary: The city said FPL had restored power to 50,000 customers countywide by Sunday morning, with more coming online. The airport is open but flights are returning to normal slowly, and the Salvation Army is serving free meals at four sites.

news.title: Parks and community centers closed after Isaias
news.summary: City of Pensacola parks stay closed until inspected, and community centers canceled programs for Monday. Gull Point Resource Center and Park took major damage, and Osceola Golf Course will be closed for several days.

news.title: Isaias leaves 2 dead after Category 2 landfall near Destin
news.summary: Per the headline, the storm killed two people and caused widespread outages. Landfall came late Friday, Oct 9, near Destin.

news.title: Isaias cancels and postpones Pensacola-area games
news.summary: A Florida State vs Auburn baseball exhibition at Blue Wahoos Stadium and a Florida State vs Mississippi State basketball exhibition at the Bay Center were canceled. Several high school football and volleyball games were also called off or postponed.

news.title: Festa Italiana moves to mid-November
news.summary: The downtown festival is now set for Nov 13 and 14 from 11 AM to 6 PM at Fountain Park, with free admission.

coverage_note: Written overnight Tuesday Oct 13 from reports dated Oct 7 to 12, so power, water and closure status may already have changed. The forecast is the National Weather Service Pensacola 7-day forecast through Oct 19; it lists no precipitation chances and describes sunny or clear skies, so rain is shown as 0 and no day 8 was available. Must Do Pensacola's weekly list, NorthEscambia.com's events page, and the Saenger and Ice Flyers sites could not be opened, so most event details are carried over from earlier checks and from the PensacolaBeach.com October list, which has no storm notes. No organizer confirmed any event after the storm, and Gonzalez and north Escambia coverage remains thin, limited to library programs already listed. No new restaurant openings or closings were found; Pelican Bar and Grill, Casa Luvia and Launch remain unconfirmed. Visit Pensacola lists Taste of the Beach on earlier dates than Must Do Pensacola does, so check before going.
